According to some sources, a prime world named '''Gith''' was the original homeworld to a race of people.<ref name="pscs-pg12">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|page=12}}, ''A Player's Guide to the Planes''</ref> The [[illithid]] empire arrived and took the populace as slaves. After some time, the slaves revolted and freed themselves. The leader of the revolt, [[Gith]], took on the name of the old homeworld in its honor.
Her people would call themselves the [[githyanki]], "Children of Gith," although it would be after her, and not after the world from which they sprung.
A splinter group formed, following [[Zerthimon]], who would call themselves [[githzerai]].<ref name="gtta46">{{b|Planescape|A Guide to the Astral Plane|pdf=17287|page=46}}</ref>

'''Glemayne''' is a world on the [[Prime Material plane]].
The world was destroyed around [[77 YFHR]], after it was overrun by [[hellcat]]s and [[hordeling]]s at the behest of a [[baatezu]] lord.
A [[voadkyn]] shaman named [[Ombidias]] was taken to [[Dis]] and tortured. He eventually escaped to find out he was the only survivor.<ref name="fm23">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=23}}</ref>

{{Quote|''What is life, but struggle? What is struggle, but conflict? What is conflict, but battle? What is Glorium, but all of the above?''|Flatnose Grim<ref name="APPttO-p18" />}}
==Description== This small gate-town consisted a number of longhouses, shipsheds, smokehouses, and workshops. They didn't bother with stockades or walls, feeling that nature provided them with sufficient defense; all they had was a wooden tower.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> The town was also lacking any inns or taverns.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="APPttO-p18" />
At the edge of Glorium stood a small temple dedicated to the [[Norse pantheon]] but primarily to [[Odin]] and the [[Norns]]. The pantheon's other members were only acknowledged in an offhand way.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="APPttO-p18" />
Like all gate-towns, Glorium was strongly influenced by the nature of the plane to which it was linked, Ysgard. It exhibited enough distinctions to prevent it from being pulled into that Outer Plane, but its inhabitants recognized that they were increasingly picking up Ysgardian habits, though they were unconcerned about this fact.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
==Geography== The land around Glorium consisted of green meadows, rolling hills, and open forests.<ref>{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Sigil and Beyond|27}}</ref> Glorium itself was nestled between towering mountains<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> on the shore of a great fjord, a little-known tributary of the [[Oceanus|River Oceanus]].<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> Most resourceful travelers preferred to reach Glorium by sailing down this fjord.<ref name="APPttO-p18" />
There was only one tangible road leading out of Glorium. Crossing through glaciers and skirting cliffs, it was a rough trail leading into the back of the [[Dwarven Mountain]]s. The road didn't see much traffic.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
===Gates=== There were two ''[[gate]]s'' near Glorium—uncommon for most gate-towns, which usually had one—with both exiting into the plane of Ysgard.<ref name="TPH-p10" /><ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> The best known of the two was a a big swirling maelstrom, referred to by locals as the '''Watergate''', which was situated near the mouth of the fjord<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> and was big enough for ships to sail through.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="TPH-p10" /> Twice a day, the Watergate reversed itself, allowing people to come through from Ysgard.<ref name="APPttO-p18" />
The second ''gate'' near Glorium was at the end of the sole road leading out from the town. By following the trail one would come to a cavern, wherein resided one of the plane-spanning roots of [[Yggdrasil]].<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> What one could classify as being among the more well-known and reliable branches of the tree.<ref name="PoC.TT-p42">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Travelogue|42}}</ref> However, there was a number of side passages within the cavern,<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="APPttO-p18" /> running deep below the surface of the Outlands,<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> some to quite unpleasant places, like the [[Caverns of Thought]] or [[Gzemnid's Realm]].<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
==Defense== Glorium had a milita of freemen known as the ''hird'', of which every resident was a member. They would quickly assemble upon the sounding of a war-horn, with one member remaining behind in the town's wooden tower to watch for incoming ships. The only time they were summoned in full was on the rare ocassions when they were being raided by the [[petitioner]]s of [[Gzemnid]] or [[Ilsensine]].<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
==Trade== The people of Glorium made their living off of fishing, hunting, and some degree of farming. They also conducted trade with the petitioners of the Dwarven Mountain, though not to a great degree, because of the treacherous nature of the road leading out to it.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
==History== At some point, a group of [[adventurer]]s from the [[Prime Material plane|Prime Material]] world of [[Toril]] came to the city of [[Sigil]], having purchased a [[map]] from a sage in [[Shadowdale]]. When the group's [[fighter]] unfolded the map they began scanning it in search of Glorium, only to quickly be corrected by his [[rogue]] ally that they were actually looking for the gate-town to [[Bytopia]].<ref name="APPttO-p2">{{Cite book/A Player's Primer to the Outlands|2}}</ref>
Later when the [[Great Modron March#History|Rogue March]] passed through Glorium, the town's inhabitants left the [[modron]]s to pass by peacefully as they marched their way to the ''portal'' to Ysgard as they had reasoned that, since the modrons weren't interested in fighting back, there wasn't any glory in fighting them.<ref>{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|62}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== The bulk of the 300 residents were living humans and petitioners of humans, strongly influenced in both appearance and attitude by the Norse pantheon.<ref name="APPttO-p18" />
They were a proud people, who highly valued notions of courtesy, honesty, and respect. They didn't take insults lightly and were not eager to forgive slights against them, instead challenging offenders to duels that would last until either blood was drawn or one of the participants fell unconsciousness. Despite this, Glorium's citizenry weren't quite as battle-crazed as the inhabitants of Ysgard.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="APPttO-p18" />
The living inhabitants of Glorium were mostly fighters eager to venture away from town to make a name for themselves, making them willful henchmen and hirelings for outsider adventurers.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />
===Notable Inhabitants=== * Flatnose Grim, the chieftain of Glorium and a human [[ranger]].<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> He was a short, bear-chested warrior who was equally renowned for his capriciousness as his strength. He often took great sport in showing the latter off by wrestling guests, bending [[horseshoe]]s, and staging contests in which one threw {{SIAdj|50|lbs.|k|long=yes}} boulders.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> * The Freki twins, a pair of ship-builders known for making very refined [[longship]]s.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> * Kostbera, the nagging wife of Flatnose Grim.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /> * Thumur, a blacksmith who made relatively affordable weapons. Some claimed he enchanted his wares, but the smith himself denied this.<ref name="TPH-p10" />
==Rumors & Legends== According to rumors, the deity Gzemnid sought to annex this town<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" /><ref name="APPttO-p18" /> and its ''gates''.<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> In relation to this rumor, some claimed that creatures in service to Gzemnid haunted the mountains,<ref name="APPttO-p18" /> having reported seeing strange creatures within the cavern. Some had also reported seeing carved markings in the cavern that could be secret signs of Gzemnid's priests.<ref name="PCS-S&B-p40-41" />

at all times. Every hour is that of a warm autumn evening. It would be the most relaxing place in the multiverse, were not the hills each as busy as a beehive on the side. |[[Mordenkainen]]{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|113}} }} ==Description== In the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model, descriptions of the Golden Hills varied primarily in the size of the "hills". Some characterized them literally as a group of seven hills nestled in the center of Dothion, the "topmost" layer of the [[Twin Paradises]]. But it was also said that [[Baervan Wildwanderer]]'s oak tree, [[Whisperleaf]], grew on the side of mountain that was joined at the top to another mountain that rose from Shurrock, the other half of the Twin Paradises. Connections to this region were the same as for the Twin Paradises, but it was said that mine shafts in [[Flandal Steelskin]]'s domain connected the Mithral Forge to digs on other planes, including [[Acheron]], [[Baator]], [[Concordant Opposition]], the [[Elemental Plane of Earth]], [[Pandemonium]], the [[Great Wheel cosmology#Inner Planes|Quasi-Elemental Plane of Minerals]], and [[Ysgard]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|109}} In the [[World Tree cosmology]] model, Golden Hills was a mildly good-aligned [[celestial plane]] connected to the trunk of the [[World Tree]]. Travel to and from other celestial planes could be accomplished via the World Tree as long as the Tree or its servants approved. The usual method of travel was journeying through the [[Astral plane]], either spiritually by ''[[astral projection]]'' or physically by using ''[[plane shift]]'' or similar magics. There was a known ''portal'' to the realm of [[Gond]] the Wonderbringer in the [[House of Knowledge (plane)|House of Knowledge]] located somewhere on or under the hill belonging to [[Flandal Steelskin]]. Flandal's forges were heated by a ''portal'' to the [[Elemental Plane of Fire]], but it is unknown whether this was a one-way or two-way portal. In the [[World Axis cosmology]], the Seven Golden Hills were considered to be scattered throughout the landscape of the [[astral dominion]] of [[Arvandor]]. The seven rolling hills rose from the vast plain, covered in golden grass. Each hill belonged to one of the gnomish deities. [[Urdlen]], the eighth member of the gnomish pantheon, made its lair in [[Hammergrim]], according to the World Tree, or in the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 399: Worm Realm|399{{th}} layer]] of the [[Abyss]], in the Great Wheel interpretation.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|174}}There is a discrepancy or possible misprint in ''[[Faiths and Pantheons]]''. On page 137 it states that Urdlen's home plane is the Golden Hills. The ''[[Player's Guide to Faerûn]]'' corrects this on page 156. All accounts agreed that everything in the home of the [[Lords of the Golden Hills]] was suffused with a polished gold hue. ==Inhabitants== The only native inhabitants of this plane were the [[deva]]s, [[solar]]s, [[planetar]]s, and other [[angel]]s that served the local gods. Gnome and [[svirfneblin]] petitioners made up the rest of the population. ==Realms== [[File:MithralForge.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Map of Mithral Forge]] * [[Baervan Wildwanderer]]'s realm was known as [[Whisperleaf]]. The name was taken from the huge oak tree atop the hill, from which Baervan cut his [[halfspear]] of the same name. It was said that the tree was actually a [[treant]] of the largest size and would attack anyone who approached it other than Baervan.{{Cite dragon/61/Gods of the Gnomes|32}} A quaint and cozy cottage was near the tree, which, despite its small appearance, was large enough to hold all his petitioners. * [[Baravar Cloakshadow]]'s realm was known as the [[Hidden Knoll]]. The Sly One set all manner of non-lethal traps, illusions, and misdirections at the entrance to his domain. It was said that anyone who got past them could have their pick of the treasures in his realm. It was also said that he changed the defenses constantly to embarrass the overconfident and ensure only the truly skilled would triumph. Petitioners lived in small [[thorp]]s strewn about the hill and beneath the surface. * [[Callarduran Smoothhands]]' realm was known as [[the Deep]] or [[Deephome]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|111}} This hill was the smallest of the seven, but the vast majority of this realm was underground. [[Svirfneblin]] petitioners had an affinity for this realm, even those that did not consider Callarduran to be their patron deity.In the [[Great Wheel cosmology]], Deephome was not one of the seven Golden Hills, but was located nearby. The seventh Hill was the Workshop, realm of the gnomish inventor god [[Nebelun]], who was not active within the Realms.
Also, Callarduran Smoothhands ''was'' considered the partron of the svirfneblin in the Great Wheel cosmology.
 It was said that despite the dense depths there were caverns of breathtaking beauty to be seen. * [[Flandal Steelskin]]'s realm was known as the [[Mithral Forge]]. Almost entirely underground, a large petitioner's city sat atop a complex of mines, tunnels, and a forge heated by [[Elemental Plane of Earth|elemental fire]]. The hill reverberated with every blow of Flandal's hammer. It was rumored to contain a subterranean river of liquid [[mithral]]. * [[Gaerdal Ironhand]]'s realm was known as [[Stronghaven]]. Heavily fortified, this hill contained a citadel that was the bulwark of defense for the rest of the plane. Gaerdal took security and protection very seriously and this realm was characterized by a utilitarian design and a distinct lack of the usual tricks, jokes, and shenanigans that were found in abundance on most of the other hills.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|110}} * [[Garl Glittergold]]'s realm was known as [[Glitterhome]]. The largest of the Golden Hills belonged to the patriarch of the pantheon, but he didn't spend much of his time in residence. He preferred to wander about the plane, often in disguise, playing practical jokes, encouraging unity and cooperation, and watching over his people. * [[Segojan Earthcaller]]'s realm was known as the [[Gemstone Burrow]]. Another realm that was mostly subterranean, the Earthfriend filled his domain with burrowing animals, and together with his petitioners they riddled this hill with earthen tunnels of all sizes that joined pleasant lairs and comfortable homes. ==Appendix== ===Notes=== {{Notes}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Bytopia}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:Celestial planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Locations in the Celestial planes]] [[Category:Locations in the World Tree planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations in Arvandor]] [[Category:Locations in the World Axis planes]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Divine realms]] [[Category:Locations in the Upper Planes]] [[Category:Locations on the World Tree]]

The '''Golden Vault''' are a secretive organization based on one of the good-aligned [[Outer Planes]], and rumored to be associated with the metallic dragons. Their motto is "Do good, no matter the cost."
The organization rights moral wrongs, supports virtuous underdogs, and handles delicate situation that local authorities won't touch. Their methods are often illegal, but support a just cause.
Despite being based on the planes, their operatives are primarily based on the [[Prime Material plane]] (although individual missions may take operatives to planar locations). Operatives monitor adventuring groups and recruit the groups as a cell of new operatives, with the recruiter acting as the cell's handler. The handler may be the only other member of the Vault that the cell knows. This compartmentalization means that no one knows enough to threaten the organization at large.
Recruited groups are given an ornate music box from their handler. Cells are couriered a new golden key at the start of each mission; opening the box with the key will have the box play a message assigning the mission and providing basic details, after which the box closes and the key vanishes.
One of the rivals of the Vault are a plane-spanning criminal organization, the [[Syndicate of Terror, Extortion, Assassination, and Larceny]] (STEAL).<ref name="kftgv171172">{{b|D&D|Keys from the Golden Vault|page=171-172}}</ref>
== Known Members == * [[Meera Raheer]], handler
== Background Information ==
* The Vault is an example of a well-worn trope involving individual cells of specialists assembled by an organization, with little knowledge of who runs the organization. Examples include ''Global Frequency'', ''Charlie's Angels'', and ''Person of Interest''.

The '''Grand Gardens''' (sometimes simply the '''Gardens''') are an area abutting [[The Lady's Ward]]'s most prestigious manors. Once attended by the [[Beautification League]] as their [[faction]] headquarters, the Gardens are currently tended by the [[Bloodroot]], an ancient clan of [[eladrin]].
An outer ring of well-tended botanical wonders surrounds an inner circle of wild vegetation, the nature of which changes on a quarterly cycle, giving Sigil one of its only indications of the passage of seasons. In spring, this manifests as a deciduous forest; in summer, a tropical jungle; in fall, a thorn forest; and in winter, a coniferous forest. The personalities of the Bloodroot also change to match the vegetation.

The '''Great Modron March''' (or simply the '''Modron March''', occasionally the '''Modron Parade''' or '''Modron Procession''') is a march of thousands of [[modron]]s, pouring out of the [[Automata]] gate to [[Mechanus]], marching around the [[Great Ring]] until the remnants arrive back in [[Mechanus]]. The purpose of the March is unknown, but it's speculated to be a way to encounter and report back on the state of the planes. It's not known how long the March takes, although the bariaur guide [[Glin]] had heard that "maybe two or three [modrons] ever make the full journey, coming home a couple of cycles later."<ref name="drag20430">{{b|Dragon|Dragon Magazine 204|page=30}}</ref>
A "cycle" in Mechanus is one full turn of the largest cog, a period lasting 17 years. Every 17 cycles (289 years), the March sets out. The confusion between 17 years and 17 cycles has led some sources to claim that the March occurs every 17 years.<ref name="polmec15">{{b|Planescape|Planes of Law|pdf=17272|nip=1|page=15, Mechanus}}</ref>
The last (scheduled) March was around [[24 YFHR]].<ref name="gmm4">{{b|Planescape|The Great Modron March|pdf=17302|page=4}}</ref><ref name="gmm69">{{b|Planescape|The Great Modron March|pdf=17302|page=69}}</ref>
After the [[Primus]] had died and [[Tenebrous]] temporarily usurped his position in [[129 YFHR]], an extremely premature March was dispatched, specifically to search for the [[Wand of Orcus]].<ref name="dg8">{{b|Planescape|Dead Gods|pdf=17297|page=8}}</ref>
== Structure ==
The March consists of at least the following:<ref name="gmm8">{{b|Planescape|The Great Modron March|pdf=17302|page=8}}</ref> * One [[quinton]] * One [[hexton]] * One [[septon]] * Four [[octon]]s * Four [[nonaton]]s * Five [[decaton]]s * 50 [[pentadrone]]s * 80 [[quadrone]]s * 405 [[tridrone]]s * 1280 [[duodrone]]s * 8640 [[monodrone]]s
This makes for 16 hierarch modrons, and 10,455 base modrons, for a grand total of 10,471 modrons.
The March begins in Automata. The modrons march around the Outlands clockwise, visiting each of the gate-towns in turn. Once they reach [[Rigus]], they head for the [[rilmani]] settlement of [[Dendradis]] at the base of the [[Spire]]. From there, they head for portals to other Outer Planes.<ref name="paitmtofw34">{{b|Planescape|Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse|page=34, Turn of Fortune's Wheel}}</ref>

The '''Great Upheaval''' is an event that happened in Sigil's past, [[503 BFHR|503 years]] before Factol Hashkar's reign.
There were previously approximately 50 [[faction]]s -- some sources say 49<ref name="fm81">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=81}}</ref><ref name="pst">{{b|Torment|Planescape: Torment}}, [[Able Ponder-Thought]]</ref>, some say over 50 -- and with them each claiming their own slice of the Cage. During this time, power in the city was largely in the hands of the [[guild]]s, with factions being merely philosophical organizations. Eventually the factions broke out into all-out war. The [[Lady of Pain]] appeared before each factol with [[dabus]] to deliver a message:
{{quote|By order of the Lady of Pain, there will be but 15 factions in Sigil. Organize thy colors by a fortnight hence — or die.}}
Inside two weeks, 34 factions dissolved, and Sigillians joined the remaining 15. Some refused, or didn't make the change fast enough, resulting in a purge of over 17,000 residents. Most joined up with the most "non-faction" faction, the [[Free League]], hoping to wait there for the whole thing to blow over. This shift made the Indeps the largest faction of all time with a million members. Within 50 years, however, that number had dropped to 20,000.<ref name="fm81">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=81}}</ref><ref name="fm3">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=3}}</ref><ref name="fw64">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=64}}</ref><ref name="fw114">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=114}}</ref><ref name="fw127">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=127}}</ref>
With the factions consolidated into 15, they found their power likewise consolidated, and began edging out the guilds for control of various parts of the city. One initiative was banning any faction member from membership in a guild, a move which reduced the numbers and strength of the latter. Eventually the factions took over. A handful of the larger guilds still exist, but at a fraction of their former strength.
== Factions ==
The following factions are known to have survived the Great Upheaval. Most predated it, but a few were formalized as factions during the Upheaval itself as factions desperately tried to make sure they got out on top, and Cagers tried to find a home among the survivors:
# [[Athar]] # [[Believers of the Source]] # [[Bleak Cabal]] # [[Doomguard]] # [[Hands of Havoc|Dustmen]] # [[Fated]] # [[Fraternity of Order]] # [[Free League]] # [[Harmonium]] # [[Mercykillers]] # [[Society of Sensation]]
This leaves four positions unknown.
Anarchists have existed for a long time, but it's not sure when they were formalized as the Revolutionary League. Xaositects didn't arrive in Sigil for another 479 years. The history of the Sign of One and Transcendent Order are uncertain.
The Zactars and Communals existed in the period between the Great Upheaval and the present, but it's not certain if they were around as early as the Great Upheaval.
== Background Information == * The discrepancy in faction numbers pre-Upheaval may be because some factions, like the [[Free League]], do not consider themselves to be factions. Alternately, the number of factions may have been measured by the [[Fraternity of Order]] based on who had formally registered themselves. Some factions (Free League, [[Revolutionary League]]) would definitely not have done so. * The "Great Upheaval" is also occasionally used by denizens of [[Ravenloft]] to refer to the ''Grand Conjunction'', an event which shook up the structure of the demiplane's domains in 740 BC ([[125 YFHR]]).

{{GA}} {{Plane | image = [[File:Planes-5e.jpg|250px]] | caption = | name = Great Wheel cosmology | type = [[Cosmology]] | natives = | languages = | gravity trait = | time trait = | shape & size = | morphic = | elemental & energy traits = | alignment trait = | magical trait = | faith trait = | inhabitants = | deities = | locations = | organizations = | settlements = | usethe = | useon = }} The '''Great Wheel cosmology''' was the prevalent cosmological model in which the world of [[Toril]] was said to exist during the mid-14{{th}} century [[DR]] and the post-[[Second Sundering]] era.<ref name="DMG5e-p44">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|44}}</ref><ref name="DR54-p9">{{Cite dragon/54/Down-to-earth divinity|9}}</ref><ref group=note>[[Ed Greenwood]] created the [[Faerûnian pantheon]] by choosing deities from the first edition ''[[Deities & Demigods 1st edition|Deities & Demigods]]'' book, sometimes renaming and modifying them, with the aim of ending up with one deity for every Outer plane or Outer planar layer in what we now call the Great Wheel cosmology. In this sense, the Faerûnian pantheon was created with the Great Wheel in mind.</ref>
The Great Wheel was described as a complex, comparatively cosmopolitan place in which the gods of many worlds and pantheons mingled, the beliefs of many faiths and peoples bleeding together in a set of [[Outer Planes]] shaped predominantly by the polar forces of Law, Chaos, Good, and Evil. Thus it was that [[Lliira]] and the Greek goddess [[Hecate]] could feud over the love of the Sumerian god [[Enki]] and work at a pleasure palace operated by the Aztec gods Xochipilli and Tlazoteotl.<ref name="TotOP-4">{{Cite book/Tales of the Outer Planes|4}}</ref><ref group=note>That was in first edition, long before the debut of the [[Planescape Campaign Setting]] in 1994, which offered alternative names for many of the planes.</ref><ref name="PCS.DMG-48-64">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|48–64}}</ref> In fact, a number of alliances existed between the gods of Toril and those of other worlds, for example, between [[Mystra]] and Wee Jas of [[Oerth]],<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|167}}</ref> as well as a plot by a god of Toril ending up involving the gods of [[Krynn]].<ref>{{Cite book/Tymora's Luck}}</ref>
The actual term "Great Wheel" did not mean the cosmology as a whole until the development of the [[World Tree cosmology]] in [[1372 DR]].<ref>{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|8}}</ref><ref name="FRCS3e-p256">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|256}}</ref><ref name="PGtF-139">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|139}}</ref><ref group="note">In 3rd edition, the [[Forgotten Realms]] cosmology was [[Wikipedia:Retroactive continuity|retconned]], with the [[World Tree cosmology]] replacing the Great Wheel. The in-game explanation for the change was given in ''Die, Vecna, Die! ''which marked the end of the 2nd edition cosmology:

Though the Lady of Pain attempts to heal the damage, the turmoil spawned by Vecna's time in Sigil cannot be entirely erased. Some Outer Planes drift off and are forever lost, others collide and merge, while at least one Inner Plane runs "aground" on a distant world of the Prime. Moreover, the very nature of the Prime Material Plane itself is altered. This event shifted the realms of many deities around to group them by pantheon or theme rather than alignment. For example, in ''[[Sacrifice of the Widow]]'', [[Cavatina Xarann]] tells that [[Vhaeraun]]'s realm is in Carceri (Tarterus) and [[Eilistraee]] lives in Svartalfheim. The ''[[Player's Guide to Faerûn]]'' still uses the terms Inner and Outer planes even though they are no longer thought of as concentric spheres. </ref> By the [[Time of Troubles]], the terms "Great Wheel" or "Great Ring" meant the Outer Planes only.<ref name="PWH-p151">{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|151}}</ref> During this time, the cosmology as a whole did not require a name other than "the Planes" or "the Multiverse," as there were no formally named alternatives yet.
By the late years of the 15{{Th}} century [[DR]], some sages began to use again the Great Wheel cosmology model, while other sages preferred to use the World Tree or the [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] models.<ref name="DMG5e">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|42-43}}</ref><ref name="Jeremy">{{cite web|author=[[Jeremy Crawford]]|title=Jeremy's Twitter|url=https://twitter.com/JeremyECrawford/status/558443947815489536|accessdate=2018-01-25}}</ref> Of the three, the Great Wheel model remained the most commonly used; however, it was modified to include the planes discovered after the [[Spellplague]].<ref name="PHB5e-p300-303">{{Cite book/Player's Handbook 5th edition|300-302}}</ref>
==Basic Structure== The Great Wheel cosmology consisted of a series of somewhat concentric spheres.<ref name="DMG2ed-132">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 2nd edition|132}}</ref> In the center was the [[Prime Material plane]] containing the [[phlogiston]] with the [[crystal sphere]]s and worlds within, surrounded by an [[Ethereal plane]] (misty realms of proto-matter). Outside of the Prime and Ethereal were the [[Inner plane]]s, also called the [[Elemental plane]]s, which had their own structure based on a sphere. Then came the [[Astral plane]] which connected the worlds in the Prime Material plane to each other (bypassing the phlogiston) and also to the last sphere, the [[Outer plane]]s.<ref name="DMG5e-p46-47">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|46-47}}</ref><ref group=note>In 1994 the ''Planescape'' setting collapsed the alternate Prime Material planes into a single plane consisting of the countless crystal spheres of the [[Spelljammer: AD&D Adventures in Space|Spelljammer]] setting, star-studded orbs that each contained a planetary system. Crystal spheres included [[Realmspace]], which contained the ''[[Forgotten Realms]]'' setting; Greyspace, which contained the ''[[Oerth|Greyhawk]]'' setting, and Krynnspace, which contained the ''Dragonlance'' setting. The spheres were surrounded by the [[Phlogiston]], a many-colored chaos that was considered beyond the power of the gods.</ref> The Prime Material plane touched both the Astral plane and its Ethereal plane, though these planes did not touch one another.<ref name="PWH-p32">{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|32}}</ref> The Outer planes, also called the Planes of Power, were 16 planes arranged in a circle (the Great Wheel) defined mainly by [[alignment]] and surrounding a 17th [[neutral]] plane known as the [[Outlands]].<ref name="DMG2ed-132" /><ref name="PHB5e-p300-303"/><ref name="DMG5e-p67-68">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|67-68}}</ref>
[[Image:PlaneNavigation.png|thumb|300px|''Interconnectivity of the planes in the Great Wheel model.'']] The Inner planes were the six major elemental planes (Fire, Earth, Water, Air, Positive Energy, Negative Energy), the four para-elemental planes (Smoke, Ice, Ooze, Magma), and the eight quasi-elemental planes (Lightning, Steam, Radiance, Minerals, Vacuum, Salt, Ash, Dust). They could be thought of as being on the surface of a sphere with Positive Energy at the north pole, Negative Energy at the south pole and Fire, Earth, Water, and Air on the equator, equidistant from each other. The para-elemental planes were found on the equator between the boundaries of Fire, Earth, Water, and Air (Magma was between Fire and Earth, for example). Four of the quasi-elemental planes were found between the boundaries of Positive Energy and the four elements (Steam was between Positive Energy and Water, for example). And the other four quasi-elemental planes were between Negative Energy and the four elements (Vacuum was between Negative Energy and Air, for example).<ref name="MotP1e-22">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|22-23}}</ref> The Inner planes were surrounded by the [[Ethereal plane]]s, which connected them to the Prime Material planes.<ref name="DMG2ed-132" />
[[Demiplane]]s were planes of finite extent found within an Ethereal plane.<ref name="PWH-p32"/> They may have been the creations of extremely powerful [[wizard]]s, [[technologist]]s, or [[demigod]]s<ref name="DMG2ed-132" /> or they may have been created when a large glob of proto-matter began to pull away from its Ethereal plane and achieved separation. Demiplanes might eventually collapse in on themselves, re-merge with its parent Ethereal, or merge with an Inner plane or Prime Material plane. Each demiplane had its own rules regarding gravity, vision, magic, and material make-up.<ref name="MotP1e-21">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|21}}</ref>
==Transitive Planes== ===Ethereal Planes=== {{main|Ethereal plane}}
In the Great Wheel model, each Prime Material plane had its own Ethereal plane in which nothing was solid, including living creatures, their possessions, weapons, and armor.<ref name="MotP1e-5">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|5}}</ref> All metal became ethereal metal, flesh became ethereal flesh, stone ethereal stone, ''etc''.<ref name="MotP1e-12">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|12}}</ref> The Ethereal touched its Prime at all points and bound it to the Inner planes, but the connections were not abrupt transitions like to/from the Astral plane but rather a gradual process in what was called the Border Ethereal. If you consider the Ethereal to be an ocean, a person in the Border Ethereal would be standing in the surf near the shore, invisible to those on land but able to see them and their surroundings dimly. One could travel along the shore, staying in the surf, and step back on land at some other point or move away from the shore toward the Deep Ethereal.<ref name="MotP1e-11">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|11}}</ref> A [[Ethereal curtain|''curtain of vaporous color'']] marked the transition between the Border Ethereal and the Deep Ethereal, and each plane had its own color. After traversing the Deep Ethereal and reaching the curtain of the correct color, you would pass through to the Border Ethereal of your destination plane.<ref name="MotP1e-12" />
By use of magic (or the natural ability that some creatures were thought to have, like [[phase spider]]s) one could fade into the Ethereal and travel at will. Gravity gave a sense of up and down, but movement in any direction was equally easy and objects released hovered in place.<ref name="MotP1e-11" /> The proto-matter swirling about the Ethereal plane could be used to create [[demi-plane]]s, either through natural fluctuations in the medium or by the actions of powerful beings. The known [[Demi-plane]]s at the time were the [[Plane of Shadow|Demi-Plane of Shadow]], the [[Demi-Plane of Time]], the [[Demi-Plane of Electro-Magnetism]] and the possibly legendary [[Demi-Plane of Imprisonment]].<ref name="MotP1e-21">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|21}}</ref>
===Astral Plane=== {{main|Astral plane}} The Astral plane was described as infinite nothingness interrupted only by small islands of material that broke off from their native planes and occasional spinning columns of astral conduits (called ''wormholes'' or ''gates'' and resembling water spouts from a storm at sea). The Astral plane connected the various [[Prime Material Plane]]s with each other and to the first layers of all the Outer planes. Travel in the Astral was usually accomplished by spell, [[psionics]], device, or ''[[color pool]]'' and involved leaving your physical body behind while your astral self traveled to your destination. During this transit, a nearly unbreakable silver cord connected your astral self back to your physical body.<ref name="MotP1e-60">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|60}}</ref> When you arrived at another plane, a new physical body manifested out of local materials.<ref name="MotP1e-75">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|75}}</ref> Wormholes linked specific places in the Outer planes to each other and to fixed locations in the Primes—quicker but likely more dangerous because your physical body was transported directly to a terminus that might be inhospitable or guarded.<ref name="MotP1e-74">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|74}}</ref>
==Outer Planes== The Outer planes were organized according to alignment, which is most easily visualized as a wheel with spokes radiating from the center of true neutrality. In the diagram below, planes associated with Good (sometimes called the [[Upper planes]]) are found above the line running from Nirvana to Limbo, and Evil-associated planes (sometimes called the [[Lower planes]]) are below. Planes associated with Law are found to the left of the line running from Elysium to Hades, and Chaos-associated planes to the right. Many of the Outer planes were divided into layers—infinite sub-regions that metaphysically overlapped the other layers of the same plane.<ref name="MotP1e-76">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|76}}</ref> [[Image:GreatWheel.jpg|thumb|600px|center|The Great Wheel of the Outer Planes]] ;[[Nirvana|Nirvana/Mechanus]] :Nirvana was the plane of [[lawful neutral]]. It consisted of only one layer where everything was in perfect order: equal parts light and dark, heat and cold, and equal measures of the four elements. The entire plane was filled with interlocking wheels {{SI|1000|mi|k|long=yes}} or more in diameter slowly turning in synchronicity. Each disk had its own gravity extending in a sphere around it, enabling the surface(s) of the wheel to be inhabited.<ref name="MotP1e-84">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|84}}</ref> [[Mystra]] once made her home here<ref name="CotR-13">{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|13}}</ref> and [[Helm]]'s realm ''Everwatch'',<ref name="OHG-p181">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|181}}</ref> [[Psilofyr]]'s realm ''Mycelia'',<ref name="OHG-176">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|176}}</ref> [[Amaunator|Amaunator's]] ''Keep of the Eternal Sun'',<ref name="OHG-182">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|182}}</ref> and [[Hoar]]'s ''Doomcourt''<ref name="PP-28">{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|28}}</ref> were all on this plane.
;[[Arcadia]] :Arcadia was between [[lawful neutral]] and [[lawful good]] in alignment, known for its trees. The trees of Arcadia grew in neat forests and regimented orchards. The bark was either [[copper]], [[gold]], [[silver]], or [[iron]], and the never-falling leaves ranged from dark green to fire red. The fruit from these trees had magical properties like [[potion]]s when consumed.<ref name="MotP1e-86">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|86}}</ref> Arcadia had three layers, Abellio,<ref name="OHG-p172">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|172}}</ref> Buxenus,<ref name="OHG-p181"/> and a third layer of which very little is known, including its name.<ref name="MotP1e-86" /> See the main article for information about the inhabitants and features of Arcadia.
;[[Seven Heavens|Seven Heavens/Mount Celestia]] :Seven Heavens, also called the Seven Mountains of Goodness and Law, was the plane of [[lawful good]] alignment, home of the [[Celestial archon|archons]].<ref name="MotP1e-87">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|87}}</ref> Its seven layers (Lunia, Mecuria, Venya, Solania, Mertion, Jovar, and Chronias) were joined in such a manner that traveling deeper into the plane became an ascending journey, up mountain after mountain for example. Each layer glowed with its own color of soft light and each was unique in terrain. The Seven Heavens were the home of [[Bahamut]], [[Yondalla]], and [[Moradin]] Dwarffather.<ref name="MotP1e-88">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|88}}</ref> See the main article for information on the seven layers and their denizens.
;[[Twin Paradises|Twin Paradises/Bytopia]] :The Twin Paradises were between [[lawful good]] and [[neutral good]] in alignment.<ref name="MotP1e-89">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|89}}</ref> The two layers (Shurrock and Dothion) were described as hanging upside down from each other about {{SI|20|mi|k|long=yes}} apart (from sea level to sea level), sharing the same sky. Gravity was normal for each layer but in opposite directions. The Twin Paradises were the home of [[Garl Glittergold]], [[Baervan Wildwanderer]], [[Segojan Earthcaller]], and [[Flandal Steelskin]] of the [[gnomish]] pantheon.<ref name="MotP1e-88" /> See the main article for descriptions of each layer.
;[[Elysium]] :Elysium was the plane of [[neutral good]]. The wide, slow-moving, and mostly navigable river [[Oceanus]] flowed through all four layers (from Thalasia to Belierin to Eronia to Amoria) and then on to the Happy Hunting Grounds. Most habitation was along the fertile banks of the river, diminishing farther away.<ref name="MotP1e-90">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|90}}</ref> [[Isis]], [[Ishtar]], and [[Enlil]] all made Elysium their home.<ref name="MotP1e-91">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|91}}</ref> See the main article for more information on the layers of Elysium.
;[[Happy Hunting Grounds|Happy Hunting Grounds/Beastlands]] :Outsiders called it the Happy Hunting Grounds, but the native wildlife, most of which were sentient and capable of speech, called it the Beastlands and didn't take kindly to being hunted. This plane represented the ideals of [[neutral good]] but tended toward [[chaotic good]]. Each of the three layers (Krigala, Brux, and Karasuthra) was vast and densely forested, but included habitats for all manner of natural creatures: mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, amphibians, insects, invertebrates, and their giant varieties.<ref name="MotP1e-91" /> [[Skerrit]] the [[centaur]] god made his home here as well as the [[Beast Lord]]s.<ref name="MotP1e-92">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|92}}</ref> See the main article for information on the different layers and the "faces in the clouds".
;[[Arborea|Olympus/Arvandor/Arborea]] :Occasionally called Olympus, or Arvandor, Arborea was the plane of [[chaotic good]], home of both the Greek and Elvish pantheons. The two realms coexisted on the topmost layer of the plane at the pinnacle of their respective realms.<ref name="MotP1e-92" /> The main feature was [[Mount Olympus]], a huge mountain that linked the Greek part of the plane with the [[Prime Material Plane]]s where they were strongest.<ref name="MotP1e-72">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|72}}</ref> This astral landmark also extended to at least one layer each of [[Gehenna]], [[Hades]], and [[Tarterus]]. This plane's three layers were called, in Greek/Elvish, [[Arvandor (layer)|Olympus/Arvandor]], [[Aquallor|Ossa/Aquallor]], and [[Mithardir|Pelion/Mithardir]]. Tucked away in a corner (so to speak) was the realm of [[Nephthys]].<ref name="MotP1e-94">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|94}}</ref> See the main article for more information about this fascinating plane.
;[[Gladsheim|Gladsheim/Ysgard]] :Sometimes called Ysgard,<ref name="OHG-p140">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|140}}</ref> Gladsheim was between [[chaotic good]] and [[chaotic neutral]] in alignment and was the home of the Norse pantheon (of which [[Tyr]] was a member<ref name="CotR-18">{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|18}}</ref>) which, despite a tendency to chaotic behavior, effectively seized control of the uppermost of the three layers.<ref name="MotP1e-95">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|95}}</ref> Their realm gives the first layer its name, Asgard, followed by Muspelheim and Nidavellir.<ref name="MotP1e-94" /> Like [[Mount Olympus]] in [[Olympus]], the main feature of this plane is [[Yggdrasil]], the "World Ash", a tree that has roots and branches in the [[Prime Material Plane]]s where the Norse gods are recognized as well as Niflheim in [[Hades]].<ref name="MotP1e-72" /> Forgotten Realms deities that made their home here were [[Selûne]],<ref name="FRA-p29">{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|29}}</ref> [[Sharess]] (in her aspect as [[Bast]]),<ref name="PaP-p51">{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|51}}</ref> [[Marthammor Duin]],<ref name="OHG-p172"/> and [[Eilistraee]]<ref name="OHG-p173">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|173}}</ref>. See the main article for more information on Gladsheim.
;[[Limbo]] :Limbo was the plane of [[chaotic neutral]], home of the [[Githzerai]] and the [[Slaad]].<ref name="MotP1e-98">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|98}}</ref> This plane was supreme chaos: a twisting, quicksilver place filled with bits and pieces of rocks, trees, the four elements, entire landscapes, strong winds, and random pockets of liquid, solid, or gas. Intelligent beings could subjugate the environment around them, causing the chaos to settle into forms of his or her desire.<ref name="MotP1e-97">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition}}</ref> It was believed Limbo had five layers but they were all generally the same.<ref name="MotP1e-98" /> [[Leira]],<ref name="CotR-11">{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|11}}</ref> [[Tempus]],<ref name="CotR-15">{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|15}}</ref> and [[Fenmarel Mestarine]]<ref name="DD-135">{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|135}}</ref> made their home here.
;[[Pandemonium]] :Pandemonium was the plane between [[chaotic neutral]] and [[chaotic evil]] in alignment and had no native inhabitants but many that were either immigrants, exiles, marooned, or prisoners.<ref name="MotP1e-100">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|100}}</ref> The entire plane was made of passages and caverns seemingly carved from solid rock by the constant howling wind and wind-driven rivers.<ref name="MotP1e-99">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|99}}</ref> [[Demon]]s and [[quasit]]s lived or hid here and [[shadow demon]]s were plentiful.<ref name="MotP1e-100" /> [[Talos]] made his home here,<ref name="CotR-15" /> and temporary visitors included Loki from [[Gladsheim]] and [[Loviatar]] of [[Gehenna]].<ref name="MotP1e-101">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|101}}</ref> See the main page for more details on Pandemonium and its four known layers: [[Pandesmos]], [[Cocytus]], [[Phlegethon]], and [[Agathion (layer)|Agathion]].
;[[Abyss|The Abyss]] :The Abyss was the plane of [[chaotic evil]], home of the [[demon]]s and a seemingly limitless number of other foul monstrosities. The stronger sought to dominate the weaker and the weaker conspired to overthrow the stronger.<ref name="MotP1e-102">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|102}}</ref> It was estimated the Abyss had 666 layers but it could well have been an infinite number.<ref name="MotP1e-101" /> :{{main|Layers of the Abyss}} :The first layer was called [[Pazunia]] (after [[Pazuzu]], who was most often found there) or the Plane of Infinite Portals, or the Palace of 1,001 Closets. It was a barren land of dusty deserts scorched by a red sun.<ref name="MotP1e-101" /> See the main article for information on the myriad layers of the Abyss.
;[[Tarterus|Tarterus/Carceri]] :The plane of Tarterus was located midway between [[chaotic evil]] and [[neutral evil]] in alignment. Each known layer of Tarterus is described as a chain of glowing scarlet orbs stretching into infinity. Each orb of the top layer is the size of a Prime Material world and the orbs get smaller with each successive layer. The orbs of the "inner" layers can be imagined as nesting within the orbs of the "outer" layers like [[Wikipedia:Matryoshka doll|Matryoshka dolls]].<ref name="MotP1e-104">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|104}}</ref> See the main article for descriptions of the known layers of Tarterus. The [[Companions of the Hall]] visited this plane in the novel ''[[The Halfling's Gem]].<ref name="THG">{{Cite book/The Halfling's Gem}}</ref>
;[[Hades|Hades/Gray Waste]] :Hades, also known as the Gray Waste, was the plane of [[neutral evil]], home of the [[daemon]]s. The three layers of Hades were Oinos, Niflheim, and Pluton. Pluton is sometimes mistakenly referred to as Hades. The layers of Hades were called ''glooms'' for good reason; they were realms devoid of emotion, hope, and peace—grey land and grey sky throughout, with no sun, moon, or seasons to break the monotony.<ref name="MotP1e-105">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|105}}</ref> Here [[Anthraxus]] ruled in his mighty fortress, the [[Khin-Oin]].<ref name="MotP1e-106">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|106}}</ref> See the main article for descriptions of the glooms and their denizens.
;[[Gehenna]] :This plane was midway between [[neutral evil]] and [[lawful evil]] in alignment. Each of the four layers (Khalas, Chamada, Mungoth, and Krangath) were composed of mountains and smoky, burning volcanoes with no bases or peaks—everything was built onto or carved into the sides of these mountains and gravity was at a 45° angle with the ground. Deeper layers had less heat and volcanic activity until you got to Krangath which had no natural light or heat.<ref name="MotP1e-107">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|107-108}}</ref> See the main article for descriptions of the layers of Gehenna.
;[[Nine Hells|Nine Hells/Baator]] :The Nine Hells, also known as Baator was the plane of [[lawful evil]], home of the [[devil]]s. The nine layers were: Avernus, Dis, Minauros, Phlegethos, Stygia, Malbolge, Maladomini, Cania (spelling changed in newer sources<ref name="MM4e-61">{{Cite book/Monster Manual 4th edition|61}}</ref>), and Nessus, and each extended infinitely in all directions and had its own physical laws and properties of matter. The barriers between layers connected the lowest points of the upper layer with points very high above the surface of the next lower layer, regardless if there was a structure (like a mountain or tall tower) there or not.<ref name="Motp1e-109">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|109}}</ref> Some infamous and powerful beings made their home in Baator, such as [[Asmodeus]], [[Mephistopheles]], [[Baalzebul]], [[Belial]], [[Mammon]], and [[Tiamat]].<ref name="MotP1e-111">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|111}}</ref> See the main article for descriptions of the Nine Hells.
;[[Acheron]] :Acheron was located between [[lawful evil]] and [[lawful neutral]] in alignment and was a place where armies of the [[Outer Planes]] would come to do battle in the [[afterlife]]. The four layers (Avalas, Thuldanin, Tintibulus, and Ocanthus) each consisted of huge blocks of hard black iron-like material the size of countries that floated through air, joining for a time and then parting again. While blocks were touching, a being could move from one block to the next. Gravity pulled toward the center of each block.<ref name="MotP1e-113">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|113}}</ref> See the main article for descriptions of the layers of Acheron and the few who lived or visited there.
;[[Concordant Opposition|Concordant Opposition/Outlands]] :Concordant Opposition, also called the Friendly Opposition, the Outlands, Godsland, and simply the Land, was the plane of true [[neutral]]ity. Divine realms on this plane included the ''Caverns of Thought'', [[Ilsensine]]'s realm; the ''Court of Light'', [[Shekinester]]'s realm; ''Dwarven Mountain'', which was the realm of [[Dumathoin]], [[Vergadain]], and [[Dugmaren Brightmantle]]; [[Annam]]'s ''Hidden Realm'', ''[[Semuanya]]'s Bog'',<ref name="PSSB-p16">{{cite book | author=[[David Cook|David "Zeb" Cook]] | title=[http://www.dnd-wiki.org/wiki/Publication:Planescape_Campaign_Setting Planescape Campaign Setting (Sigil and Beyond)] | publisher=[[TSR, Inc.]] | year=1994 | pages=16-19 | isbn=1-56076-834-7 }}</ref> [[Sheela Peryroyl]]'s ''Flowering Hill'',<ref name="OHG-p175">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|175}}</ref> ''[[Thoth]]'s Estate'',<ref name="PaP-p129">{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|129}}</ref> [[Oghma]]'s ''House of Knowledge'', [[Silvanus]]'s realm of ''Summeroak'', [[Gond]]'s realm of ''Wonderhome'',<ref name="OHG-p181"/> and [[Ubtao]]'s ''Labyrinth of Life''.<ref name="PaP-p88">{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|88}}</ref>
==Inner Planes== [[File:Inner_planes-5e.jpg|thumb|250px|''The Inner Planes.'']] The four elemental planes—one each for [[Air]], [[Fire]], [[Earth (element)|Earth]], and [[Water]]—plus the two energy planes—one for [[positive energy]] and one for [[negative energy]]—made up the six major Inner planes. Between each pair of adjacent elemental planes was a para-elemental plane. The eight quasi-elemental planes were found between the four elemental planes and the two energy planes. The four para- and eight quasi-elemental planes added up to twelve minor planes for a total of eighteen Inner planes. Each plane was made up of primarily one type of matter, but pieces of other Inner planes may have found their way in (or been brought in by powerful forces). One thing all Inner planes had in common was that they were all hostile to lifeforms from outside, particularly from the [[Prime Material Plane]]s.<ref name="MotP1e-22" />
===Elemental Planes=== ;[[Elemental Plane of Air]] :This plane was the most hospitable to beings from the Primes because the substance of the plane was breathable and travel was fairly easy. The whole plane looked like the bluest sky on a summer day<ref name="MotP1e-31">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|31}}</ref> with only the occasional cloud or storm indicating the intrusion of some other element into the constant wind that was the Plane of Air.<ref name="MotP1e-32">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|32}}</ref> Pieces of solid matter floated in this realm and became home to other-planer creatures. The open space belonged to the [[air elemental]]s.<ref name="MotP1e-31" /> [[Bahamut]] was thought to have a citadel here, as well as many other deities of various pantheons. [[Akadi]], the queen of free-willed elementals was said to dwell in ''The Great Funnel'', within a huge maelstrom able to swallow the known world.<ref name="OHG-p181" /><ref name="MotP1e-35">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|35}}</ref>
;[[Elemental Plane of Fire]] :The Plane of Elemental Fire was a hellish place, filled with all manner and color of flame from the candle to the white-hot glow of heated steel, all burning without fuel and radiating light and heat at maximum levels.<ref name="MotP1e-36">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|36}}</ref> Most unprotected matter was quickly consumed by the flames but pockets of other elements could survive in "cold spots" where the temperature was near that of a hot Prime desert.<ref name="Motp1e-38">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|38}}</ref> The evil [[efreet]] and their fabled [[City of Brass]] resided here. Also the dwarf-like [[azer]] mined the basalt rocks that survived the heat for metals for their craft. [[Kossuth]], the tyrant-king of the fire elementals dwelt in his palace at the center of his realm<ref name="Motp1e-40">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|40}}</ref> called ''The Crimson Pillar''.<ref name="OHG-p181"/><ref>[[Monte Cook]], [[William W. Connors]] (1998). ''[http://www.dnd-wiki.org/wiki/The_Inner_Planes The Inner Planes], pp. 47, 49.'' [[TSR, Inc.]] ISBN 9-780786-907366.</ref>
;[[Elemental Plane of Earth]] :More inhospitable than even the Plane of Fire, the Plane of Elemental Earth was so solid that movement was nearly impossible unless a traveler could find a pocket of some less dense element or use magic to force an opening or permit them to walk through solid material.<ref name="MotP1e-41">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|41}}</ref> Without some protection, a non-native being would be caught like a fly in [[amber]] under tremendous pressure from the surrounding rock and without air to breathe or light to see.<ref name="MotP1e-42">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|42}}</ref> Inhabitants of this plane included [[xorn]], [[crysmal]], and the [[dao]]. [[Grumbar]], the largest and most powerful Earth [[elemental]],<ref name="MotP1e-45">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|45}}</ref> resided in ''The Great Mountain''.<ref name="OHG-p181" /> [[Ogremoch]], the prince of evil earth creatures, had his own flat-topped mountain inside the largest pocket of vacuum known to exist in the plane.<ref name="MotP1e-45" /> The only deity from the Realms to make his home here was [[Geb]]<ref name="MotP1e-41" /> in his ''Caverns Under the Stars''.<ref name="OHG-p173" />
;[[Elemental Plane of Water]] :An ocean without a surface, the Plane of Elemental Water had uniform pressure in all directions and felt like being several feet below the surface of a typical body of water in a Prime Material Plane, and indeed was illuminated with the same soft light of that depth. The salinity of the water varied depending on proximity to the Negative Energy plane—pure salt at the boundary with the quasi-elemental Plane of Salt, briny as you moved away, becoming pure and fresh in the middle, then getting warmer and more agitated as you approached the quasi-elemental Plane of Steam. Pockets of the other elements could be found here, but travelers that required air to breathe needed to make other arrangements. Inhabitants of this plane included [[water weird]]s, [[nereid]]s, [[triton]]s, and the [[marid]].<ref name="MotP1e-46">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|46}}</ref> [[Istishia]] made his home here<ref name="MotP1e-50">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|50}}</ref> in a realm called the ''Sea of Timelessness''.<ref name="OHG-p181" /> ''The Murky Depths'' was the realm of [[Blibdoolpoolp]].<ref>[[Monte Cook]], [[William W. Connors]] (1998). ''[http://www.dnd-wiki.org/wiki/The_Inner_Planes The Inner Planes], p. 55.'' [[TSR, Inc.]] ISBN 9-780786-907366.</ref> ''Shelluria'' was the realm of [[Eadro]] and [[Persana]].<ref>[[Monte Cook]], [[William W. Connors]] (1998). ''[http://www.dnd-wiki.org/wiki/The_Inner_Planes The Inner Planes], p. 56.'' [[TSR, Inc.]] ISBN 9-780786-907366.</ref>
===Energy Planes=== ;[[Positive Energy plane]] :Also known as the Positive Material plane and the Plane of Life, every atom of this plane vibrated with intense energy and produced light across a wide spectrum. An unprotected traveler, if continuously exposed to the energies of this plane, would at first be healed of any wounds, then the cells of the body would quickly reach their maximum potential and then explode and become part of the plane, all in a matter of minutes. All non-magical or non-living material was quickly destroyed.<ref name="MotP1e-54">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|54}}</ref> The only known inhabitants of this plane were the inscrutable [[xag-ya]] which seemed mindless by Prime Material plane standards, but must have had some intelligence because they could act as a local guide or a guardian when summoned to other planes.<ref name="MMII-128">{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|128}}</ref> Where the Positive Energy plane metaphysically intersected with the four major elemental planes, Air, Fire, Earth, and Water, it created the quasi-elemental planes of Lightning, Radiance, Minerals, and Steam respectively.<ref name="MotP1e-54" />
;[[Negative Energy plane]] :Also known as the Negative Material plane or the Plane of Death, everything in this plane sucked in all matter and energy creating a cold, pitch dark realm with structures made up of physical, solid blackness. Any unprotected visitor would quickly sicken, shrivel up, and die in mere minutes. Magical light sources could barely penetrate the darkness and non-magical material collapsed into dust and joined the black. Many [[undead]] drew their animating force from the Negative Energy plane which allowed them to drain life force from the living.<ref name="MotP1e-54" /> The only known inhabitants of this plane were the mysterious [[xeg-yi]], analog to the xag-ya in the Positive Energy plane, and a species of "energy vulture" called the [[trilloch]]s which may have originated on a demi-plane that got absorbed.<ref name="FF1e-89">{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|89}}</ref> Where the Negative Energy plane metaphysically intersected with the four major elemental planes, Air, Fire, Earth, and Water, it created the quasi-elemental planes of Vacuum, Ash, Dust, and Salt respectively.<ref name="MotP1e-54" />
===Para-Elemental Planes=== ;[[Great Conflagration|Para-Elemental Plane of Smoke]] :Between the planes of elemental Air and elemental Fire was the plane of para-elemental Smoke, also called '''plane of Ash''' or the '''Great Conflagration'''.<ref name="DMG5e-p53">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|53}}</ref> It appeared as a cloud of foul-smelling fog which got a little more pleasant as you approached the plane of Air, or hotter and more luminous as you moved toward the plane of Fire. Smoke particles made breathing difficult to the point of asphyxiation so travelers needed to be prepared or death was delayed only as long as you could hold your breath. Pockets of Air were a welcome relief. Pockets of Fire looked like free-floating [[fireball]]s. Using the sphere model discussed above, the para-elemental plane of Smoke touched the planes of Air, Fire, Lightning, Radiance, Vacuum, and Ash, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-51">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|51}}</ref> [[Ehkahk]], the Smoldering Duke, lived in the [[Choking Palace]] and proclaimed himself ruler of the smoke [[mephit]]s.<ref name="PCS.DMG-32">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|32}}</ref>
;[[Fountains of Creation|Para-Elemental Plane of Magma]] :Between the planes of elemental Fire and elemental Earth was the plane of para-elemental Magma, also known as the '''Fountains of Creation'''.<ref name="DMG5e-p55">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|55}}</ref> It was a long sea of molten lava that thinned out and became gaseous toward the plane of Fire, or thickened until it became solid rock toward the plane of Earth. Breathing difficulty went from bad to worse in the same manner. Pockets of Fire would be bubbles of elemental Fire and the thin gasses from that plane. Pockets of Earth were pillars of [[granite]] or rough-cut stone floating in the magma. The para-elemental plane of Magma touched the planes of Fire, Earth, Radiance, Minerals, Ash, and Dust, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-51" /> [[Chilimba]], First General of the Cauldron, Master of All Mephits, claimed rulership over the entire plane from his stronghold [[Caldera]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-33">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|33}}</ref>
;[[Swamp of Oblivion|Para-Elemental Plane of Ooze]] :Between the planes of elemental Earth and elemental Water was the plane of para-elemental Ooze, also known as the '''Swamp of Oblivion'''.<ref name="DMG5e-p54">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|54}}</ref> Close to Earth the rocks and dirt took on a clammy dampness. As you moved toward Water, the density decreased to a [[quicksand]]-like state and then thinned out to muddy silt. Spells and devices that provided ''water breathing'' capability worked in this plane also. Pockets of Water would form an irregular bubble in the muck. Pockets of Earth were solid nuggets suspended in the ooze. The para-elemental plane of Ooze touched the planes of Earth, Water, Minerals, Steam, Dust, and Salt, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-51" /> Ooze was the location of [[Ghaunadaur]]'s realm, the ''Cauldron of Slime''.<ref name="DD-18">{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|18}}</ref> The only other name that survives in lore related to this plane is [[Bwimb]],<ref name="PCS.DMG-33" /> another possible prince of para-elemental evil.<ref name="MotP1e-53">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|53}}</ref>
;[[Frostfell (plane)|Para-Elemental Plane of Ice]] :The plane of para-elemental Ice, also known as the '''Frostfell''',<ref name="DMG5e-p57">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|57}}</ref> was found between the planes of elemental Water and elemental Air. Scattered icebergs marked the border with Water, eventually becoming solid ice broken by fissures and caverns until finally jutting into the plane of Air as ice cliffs. This plane shared the restrictively solid nature of the plane of Earth. Inadequately protected travelers would soon find themselves preserved for all time in sheer ice. Pockets of Water took the form of an underground lake while pockets of Air would form ice caverns of any shape or size. The para-elemental plane of Ice touched the planes of Water, Air, Steam, Lightning, Salt, and Vacuum, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|52}}</ref> [[Cryonax]], the prince of evil cold-using creatures, built his massive castle of ice, [[rock crystal]], and glass on this plane<ref name="FF1e-31">{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|31}}</ref> and named it the [[Chiseled Estate]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-34">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|34}}</ref>
===Positive Quasi-Elemental Planes=== ;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Lightning]] :Where the Positive Energy plane intersected with the plane of elemental Air, it created the quasi-elemental plane of Lightning, also called the plane of Storms, the Vengeful Land, or the Great Illumination.<ref name="PCS.DMG-34" /> At the border with Air was a continual thunderstorm with a constant barrage of lightning bolts arcing between ominously dark clouds. The atmosphere was filled with the sharp tang of ozone and a deafening cacophony of thunderclaps. All form of electrical discharge could be found here: lightning bolts, ball lightning, sheet lightning, static shocks and the gentle glow of [[wikipedia:en:St. Elmo's fire|St. Elmo's fire]]. It is said that quasi-elemental creatures cavorted amid the chaos. At the border with the Positive Energy plane stood the mysterious ''Tower of Storms'',<ref name="PCS.DMG-34" /> gateway to a continuous torrent of electrical power that issued from a wall of pure brilliance.<ref name="MotP1e-55">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|55}}</ref> Following the sphere model discussed above, the quasi-elemental plane of Lightning touched the planes of Positive Energy, Air, Radiance, Smoke, Steam, and Ice, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Radiance]] :Between the Positive Energy plane and the plane of elemental Fire was the plane of quasi-elemental Radiance where all manner of flame and fire burned at its brightest and hottest. Every color of combustion could be found here in a dazzling display seen nowhere else, and the creatures were equally brilliant. As you approached the Positive Energy plane, spheres, walls, and lines of prismatic force crisscrossed the plane as the light became sharper and more crystalline until finally blending into the coruscating whiteness of blinding intensity that indicated you had reached the border. Standing at the border was a tower of blue light called the [[Heart of Light]] that was rumored to be a place of great healing.<ref name="PCS.DMG-35">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|35}}</ref> In addition to the precautions necessary to travel the Plane of Fire, eye protection was needed to prevent permanent blindness while in this plane.<ref name="MotP1e-55" /> The quasi-elemental plane of Radiance touched the planes of Positive Energy, Fire, Lightning, Smoke, Minerals, and Magma, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Minerals]] :Between the planes of Positive Energy and elemental Earth was the plane of quasi-elemental Minerals. Upon crossing the border from the Plane of Earth, the entropy-fighting influence of the Positive Energy plane manifested in growing veins of crystal and metal-bearing ore permeating the rock, which itself became black [[marble]]. All manner of [[gem]]s and [[:Category:Metals|metals]] aggregated in their pure forms and laced the marble, becoming increasingly fragile and vibrating with energy until finally shattering at the fluctuating cliff-face border with the Positive Energy plane.<ref name="MotP1e-55" /> Near the border was the ''Tower of Lead'', said to contain the most magnificent forge in the multiverse, where master craftsmen sometimes would risk death to perfect their art.<ref name="PCS.DMG-36">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|36}}</ref> In addition to all the difficult and deadly conditions of the Plane of Earth, this plane presented even more challenges. Sharp crystalline edges could cut travelers not native to this plane or elemental Earth as they passed through. Likewise the delicate insect-like inhabitants were beautiful jeweled creatures with sharp angular features.<ref name="MotP1e-56">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|56}}</ref> By far the greatest danger to any being not native this plane was ''fossilization''. The longer one stayed in this plane, the greater the chance the forces acting on the minerals would turn you to stone (if you were lucky) or transform you into crystal, gemstones, or gold-veined granite. Magical protection from petrification did not prevent fossilization. On top of that, any crystal that formed in the intense pressure and zero gravity of the Plane of Minerals was almost certain to shatter when brought into a plane with gravity and normal atmospheric pressure.<ref name="MotP1e-57">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|57}}</ref> The quasi-elemental plane of Minerals touched the planes of Positive Energy, Earth, Radiance, Magma, Steam, and Ooze, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Steam]] :Where the Positive Energy plane intersected with the plane of elemental Water, it created the quasi-elemental plane of Steam. The temperature of this plane varied from cool to near boiling, creating the conditions for all varieties of mist, fog, and vapor. The entire plane was suffused with a soft glow which eventually became a brilliant glare at the border with the Positive Energy plane.<ref name="MotP1e-55" /> Near the border was the strangely named [[Tower of Ice]] which was used by alchemists as a laboratory to enhance potion brewing.<ref name="PCS.DMG-36" /> Air-breathing, lung-using creatures found it difficult to get enough air from the muggy water vapor and were effectively ''slowed'' by water gathering in the lungs. Overall, this was the most hospitable of the Positive quasi-elemental planes.<ref name="MotP1e-56" /> Using the sphere model discussed above, the quasi-elemental plane of Steam touched the planes of Positive Energy, Water, Minerals, Ooze, Lightning, and Ice, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
===Negative Quasi-Elemental Planes=== ;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Vacuum]] :Between the Negative Energy plane and the plane of elemental Air was the plane of quasi-elemental Vacuum. As in other Inner planes, standard physics did not apply to this plane; as the air got thinner moving toward the Negative Energy plane the temperature and pressure remained the same even when the region of perfect vacuum was reached—there was just nothing there.<ref name="MotP1e-57" /> Spells that offered protection from the elements did not protect from the ''lack'' of all elements. Even beings from neighboring planes could not survive for long as they began to consume their own essence to stay alive.<ref name="MotP1e-58">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|58}}</ref> The ambient light radiating from the Plane of Air faded to absolute black at the border with the Negative Energy plane,<ref name="MotP1e-57" /> and there is where the [[Doomguard]] built a structure called [[Citadel Exhalus]], Portal of the Last Breath.<ref name="PCS.DMG-37">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|37}}</ref> Creatures of invisible force flitted through the gloom, but for what purpose no one has ever discovered.<ref name="MotP1e-58">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|58}}</ref> The quasi-elemental plane of Vacuum touched the planes of Negative Energy, Air, Smoke, Ash, Ice, and Salt, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Ash]] :Between the planes of Negative Energy and elemental Fire was the plane of quasi-elemental Ash. Moving from the Plane of Fire, the last embers died out leaving the cold remnants of combustion hanging in the gloomy atmosphere. The temperature dropped quickly to a bone-chilling cold, all light from the Fire plane was rapidly blocked from view, and the ash steadily thickened toward the Negative Energy plane until it ended in a gray wall in the darkness at the border.<ref name="MotP1e-57" /> Vision was limited and breathing impossible without assistance of some sort. This plane would leech the warmth out of any creature with a body temperature above freezing, especially natives of Fire, Smoke, and Magma which would die in a matter of minutes.<ref name="MotP1e-58" /> Creatures of Ash shunned warmth because their bodies could explode into lumps of ash if brought to room temperature.<ref name="MotP1e-59">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|59}}</ref> Another of the [[Doomguard]]'s strongholds, the skull-shaped [[Citadel Cavitius]], was here at the border with the Plane of Death, but it was taken over by the [[lich]] [[Vecna]] long ago. They subsequently built a replacement and named it the [[Crumbling Citadel]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-37" /> The quasi-elemental plane of Ash touched the planes of Negative Energy, Fire, Magma, Dust, Smoke, and Vacuum, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Dust]] :Where the Negative Energy plane intersected with the plane of elemental Earth it created the quasi-elemental plane of Dust, home of the [[dune stalker]]s, [[sandling]]s, and [[sandman|sandmen]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-38">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|38}}</ref> From the border with the Plane of Earth, the earth and rock cracked and split into smaller and smaller pieces, losing cohesion and variation until nothing was left except fine sand. At the same time the pressure experienced in the Earth plane was reduced to normal but there was still no breathable atmosphere. Continuing on, the grains got finer and farther apart, the empty blackness between the dust motes grew until finally all motes dispersed and only Negative Energy was left.<ref name="MotP1e-57" /> Here the [[Doomguard]] built their favorite tower, the [[Citadel Alluvius]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-38" /> The disassociation and dispersal properties of this plane acted on anything solid that lacked protection. In a matter of minutes, non-native items and creatures, including beings from neighboring Inner planes that were at least partially solid, would break down and drift apart long past the point where life was sustainable.<ref name="MotP1e-58" /> The quasi-elemental plane of Dust touched the planes of Negative Energy, Earth, Ooze, Salt, Magma, and Ash, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
;[[Quasi-Elemental Plane of Salt]] :Between the Negative Energy plane and the plane of elemental Water was the plane of quasi-elemental Salt. Entering this plane from the Plane of Water, the brine overwhelmed the merely salty water and quickly solidified into hard crystalline lumps of salt. All water was soon absorbed or evaporated and the lumps joined to form a solid block of salt which continued until it ended in a great cliff overlooking the Negative Energy plane. At the border, carved out of the salt cliffs, was the [[Doomguard]] stronghold [[Citadel Sealt]].<ref name="PCS.DMG-38" /> All unprotected beings containing water quickly dehydrated until their desiccated remains were encased in salt.<ref name="MotP1e-58" /> Denizens of this plane feared water in any quantity because it would start to dissolve them or violently shatter them if immersed.<ref name="MotP1e-59" /> The quasi-elemental plane of Salt touched the planes of Negative Energy, Water, Ice, Vacuum, Ooze, and Dust, and could be reached directly through the Ethereal plane.<ref name="MotP1e-52" />
==Revision== When sages of the late 15{{Th}} century began to use the Great Wheel model again, they revised it to include the new planes discovered after the Spellplague and normally associated with the World Axis model.<ref name="DMG5e"/><ref name="Jeremy"/><ref group=note>Although there is no in-game explanation for the addition of those planes to the Great Wheel, it has been said by 5th-edition developers that the cosmological models described in the 5th-edition's Dungeon's Master Guide are creations of sages of diverse mortal worlds, implying that the Great Wheel was revised at some point.</ref>
The [[Elemental Chaos]] was considered to be the farthest extent of the inner planes, a hostile and unknown plane where all the elemental planes were combined. Some speculated it was home to strange elemental creatures.<ref name="DMG5e-52-53">{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|52-53}}</ref>
The [[Feywild]] and the [[Shadowfell]] were considered to be [[parallel plane]]s to the Prime Material, extreme echoes of the worlds of the Prime much like in the World Axis model. Those planes replaced the Plane of Faerie and the Plane of Shadow of the earlier version of the Great Wheel model.<ref name="PHB5e-p300-303"/>

'''Greyhawk''' is a [[Dungeons & Dragons]] Campaign Setting. Although D&D 3rd Edition was the first edition to introduce a default setting, putting ''Greyhawk'' in that place of honor, it could be argued that it was also the default setting of AD&D's 1st Edition. ''Greyhawk'' is, in many ways, what comes to mind when people think of a generic D&D world.
Outside of Dave Arneson's Blackmoor, ''Greyhawk'' was the first D&D setting, largely the creation of Gary Gygax. Castle Greyhawk (for its dungeons) and the nearby city of Greyhawk (to live, sell treasure, and acquire new gear) were initially all he designed, and further design largely happened as needed, leaving most of the world blank.
''Greyhawk'' takes place on the world of [[Oerth]] in [[w:c:spelljammer:Greyspace|Greyspace]]. As the name implies, it was originally intended to be a fantasy variant of Earth, with a map drawn on top of a map of North America. Eventually freelance artist Darlene Pekul designed a new map of Oerth, which Gygax loved enough to officially adopt.
The world has an axial tilt of 30°, making its seasons more extreme than Earth's. Oddly, Oerth is one of a few systems where the planet is truly at the center of the solar system, and the sun orbits around it.
Despite having a map to explore, most of the world remained undefined, leaving it up for individual DMs to customize various nations and settlements for their own home games.
