Before the [[Great Upheaval]], it was the '''guilds''' who ran the city of Sigil, powerful and well-organized groups. Their power since then has greatly diminished, and most have withered away.<ref name="fw19">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=19}}</ref> With the dissolution of the factions in the wake of the [[Faction War]], however, the guilds have once again started to rise to prominence.<ref name="dmg2-198">{{b|D&D|Dungeon Master's Guide 2|pdf=144108|page=198}}</ref>
Many of the guilds kept their headquarters in the [[Guildhall Ward]], which gave the Ward its name. Like factions, guilds have symbols that members wear as identification. They also typically have annual membership dues to help pay the rent on their headquarters.
== History ==
At one point in Sigil's history, the guilds ran the city. They were reliable and safe islands of stability in the constant infighting among the city's 50 factions.<ref name="fw20">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=20}}</ref> After the [[Great Upheaval]], however, the pendulum swung: with fewer factions, they were able to consolidate their power, and began edging the guilds out.
The collapse of the guilds was caused by a lack of [[faction]] support, as the newly-empowered factions saw the guilds as their biggest threat. The claim was that the guilds fostered divided loyalties.<ref name="itc87">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|nip=1|page=87}}</ref><ref name="fw20">{{b|Planescape|Faction War (book)|alt=Faction War|pdf=17299|page=20}}</ref> The killing blow was when the factions declared that no faction member could also be a member of any guild or club.<ref name="tftis20">{{b|Planescape|Tales from the Infinite Staircase|pdf=17291|nip=1|page=20}}</ref> While the Lady didn't say a word, it was nonetheless clear that the guilds were no longer welcome in the city.
Eventually, most of the guilds relocated or withered away. Without the presence of the guilds, the [[Market Ward]] and [[Guildhall Ward]] became less distinguishable from each other, and most modern Cagers consider them two halves of the same whole, with [[Duskgate Road]] forming the informal boundary between them<ref name="itc87">{{b|Planescape|In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|pdf=17274|nip=1|page=87}}</ref>

Gray land and gray sky throughout, with no sun, moon or seasons to break the monotony. Any color other than shades of gray would be obvious against the background but would fade to gray in a week or two. And like bright colors, beings would begin to fade also. At first they would feel the drain of emotions leaving only sadness, ennui, and defeatism. In a [[tenday]] or two they would be trapped in Hades and their existence would begin to fade until finally they became [[Soul larva|larvae]]. Hades was a unique plane, as described by the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model, because it not only joined to adjacent planes in the Great Wheel, it also held the foundation of [[Mount Olympus]] and the roots of [[Yggdrasil]] the World Ash. These two planar artifacts connected Hades to [[Olympus]], in the [[Arvandor (layer)|first layer]] of [[Arborea]], and [[Ysgard]] respectively, allowing travel between Hades, the [[Upper planes]], and Alternate [[Prime Material Plane]]s{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|72}} without going through the [[Astral Plane]], much like the [[World Tree]] in the [[World Tree cosmology]].{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}} ===Oinos=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Oinos}} The first layer of Hades was named for the lord of the daemons (the [[Oinodaemon]]), [[Anthraxus]] the Decayed. Oinos was the land of disease with stunted and withered plants amid gray rocky terrain. The river [[Styx]] flowed through this layer and there were portals to [[Tarterus]], [[Gehenna]], and [[Concordant Opposition]] that looked like huge spinning metal coins, visible for miles, often guarded by iron fortresses. Anyone walking this land or floating on the river Styx had a chance of contracting a major disease. Many of the daemons and some of the other creatures from the lower middle planes who were immune to disease made their home here. ===Niflheim=== {{Main|Niflheim}} Compared to Oinos, the terrain in the second layer was rougher, like foothills, with cooler temperatures, healthier vegetation including pine trees, and no disease. Everything was cloaked in dreary fog and mist, limiting vision to about a hundred feet (thirty meters). [[Yggdrasil]]'s roots reached Niflheim, connecting it to [[Gladsheim#Asgard|Asgard]] in [[Gladsheim]]. The goddess [[Shar]] once maintained an abode here.{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|138}}{{Cite book/Netheril: Empire of Magic/The Winds of Netheril|55}} ===Pluton=== {{Main|Pluton}} The lowest level of Hades contained the base of [[Mount Olympus]], a direct conduit through the [[Astral Plane]] to the plane of [[Arborea]]. The gray motif continued throughout this layer but most of the vegetation was black willow trees and dry, dying poplars. ==Inhabitants== The [[daemon]]s were the presumed rulers of Hades, but were actually outnumbered by the bird-like [[diakk]]{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|50}} and the [[greater deity|greater powers]] had no trouble carving out realms for themselves. Factions of [[demodand]]s carried on a low-level insurgency, sniping at the daemons but generally avoiding large-scale conflict that might attract the attention of the resident deities. Also known to inhabit all layers of Hades were [[achaierai]],{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|9}} [[nightmare]]s, [[mephit]]s{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|64}} and [[night hag]]s.{{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|73}} ==Afterlife== [[File:Yggdrasil2Hades.jpg|right|thumb|300px|The layers of Hades, Mount Olympus, and Yggdrasil]] {{Main|Afterlife}} Most souls that arrived in Hades Having different opinions from your neighbor means discord, so it's best if everyone thinks the same way. By force, if necessary. == History == The Harmonium began in [[374 BFHR]] as an adventuring party on the Prime world of [[Ortho]], setting a goal to "rid the country of chaos and bring peace to the land." Unlike most such parties, they actually did it. Gradually, they would bring peace to the entire world (whether it wanted it or not). Occasionally chaos would rampage across the land, and they tracked these to demonic incursions from the [[Outer Planes]]. {{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=90}} Once they discovered the Outer Planes, it wasn't long before they found their way to [[Sigil]].{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=33}} * [[74 BFHR]]: The Harmonium arrive in Sigil at approximately this time.{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=90}} * [[77 YFHR]]: [[Omar]] becomes [[factol]] of the Harmonium... and immediately tries to disband the [[faction]] and shut down the [[City Barracks]]. Omar is revealed to be an [[Revolutionary League|Anarchist]]. The Harmonium later insists they simply let him think he was in charge so he'd reveal himself. The [[Mercykillers]] execute him after a brief trial, and he becomes a hero and martyr for the Anarchists.{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=114}} * [[107 YFHR]]: [[Sarin]] arrives in [[Sigil]] around this time.{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=91}} * [[122 YFHR]]: [[Sarin]] becomes [[factol]] of the Harmonium around this time.{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=92}} * The loss of [[Namausus]] to [[Mechanus]] seems to have happened relatively recently -- within the last decade or so -- but details are unknown. * [[127 YFHR]]: An attempt to have [[Fortitude]] [[Cosmic realignment|slide]] into [[Arcadia]] goes awry, nearly ending with the city falling into [[Baator]].{{b|Planescape|Fires of Dis|pdf=17273|page=63}} Previous factols: * Unnamed factol (killed by a Xaositect hourglass, not long after the faction arrived in Sigil){{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=152}} == Philosophy == Peace is our goal. But if it takes a little war to get others to se things the Harmonium way, so be it. That's how we'll reach our golden harmony. === Branches === Not all the people of Ortho embraced the Harmonium ethos. The dissenters called themselves the [[Riven]]. Rather than commit genocide, the Harmonium offered the Riven exile, an offer which was accepted. The Riven traveled to the [[Elemental Plane of Air]] where they established a community called [[Blurophil]] on a massive metal disk.{{b|Planescape|Tales from the Infinite Staircase|pdf=17291|nip=1|page=75-76}} == Role == The Hardheads run the [[City Barracks]]. == Membership == : ''See also:'' [[List of Harmonium members]] ; '''[[Namer]]s''' Namers who have completed basic training at the Harmonium camp on [[Buxenus]] become '''Notaries'''. Notaries fall into five ranks, based on length of service. Those fresh out of training are Notary Ones, while those who have been around a while are Notary Fives. * ''Benefits'': All Hardheads can use ''charm person'' 1/day. Priests gain access to ''[[dictate]]'' as a 2nd level spell. ''Known Namers'': * Notary Three {{NPC|Guin Rhond||||||Harmonium|}}{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|nip=1|page=63}} ; '''[[Factotum]]s''' Every six months, any Notary who decides to become an officer receives advanced training, with graduates becoming '''Measures'''. Like Notaries, they rank from Measure Ones to Measure Fives. * ''Benefits'': Measures at 4th level gain a +1 bonus to attack with a weapon of their choice. ''Known Measures'': * {{NPC|Diana the Guardian|planar|female|human|enchanter|12|Harmonium|ln}}{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|nip=1|page=93}} * Measure Three {{NPC|Ebb Creakknees||male|?|fighter||Revolutionary League|}}{{b|Torment|Planescape: Torment}} ; '''[[Factor]]s''' Factors are known as '''Movers'''. As with Notaries and Measures, Movers have five sub-ranks. * ''Benefits'': At 7th level, Movers gain a +3 bonus to saves against fear or emotion-related spells and abilities. Divinely morphic | element-energy-WT = Mixed{{Cite dragon/291/Sage Advice|108}} | alignment-WT = Mixed | magical-WT = | faith-WT = Mild | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = {{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|156-157}}{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|141}} | inhabitants = yes | deities = | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = | based = | usethe = | useon = }} '''Heliopolis''' was the [[divine realm]] of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|89}} It was jointly ruled by the powers [[Ra]], [[Isis]] and [[Osiris]], and also housed [[Horus]]. ==Cosmography== Under the [[Great Wheel cosmology|Great Wheel]] model, Heliopolis was a single [[divine realm]] that resided on [[Buxenus]], the second layer of the plane of [[Arcadia]]. Under the [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]] model, it was considered to be a [[Neutral Planes|Neutral Plane]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|258}} ==Geography== ===Great Wheel=== [[File:Heliopolis-GreatWheelDivision.png|thumb|273px|''The three equally divided realms of Heliopolis, according to the Great Wheel.'']] Under the Great Wheel cosmology, the realm was said to be an immense burning desert of bright sand that was laid out like a triangle, divided into three equally sized domains. It was touched at every corner by a scorching sun, which was guided across the sky by Ra's solar barge ''[[Matet|Manjet]]''.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|86}}{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|19}} This was in contrast to the rest of Arcadia, which received light from the '''Orb of Day and Night''', though the time of day for both coincided. When the time for day to end came Ra's barge became a funeral barge, referred to as ''Mesketet'', and briefly provided light to the realm of Osiris. Whenever the sun faded in Heliopolis the temperature would drop dramatically. However, the overall temperature varied between the three domains that each deity governed. The domain of Ra was the hottest of three, the heat striking even indoors and in shadowed area. Fauna were almost never seen out during the day in his realm, due to the unbearable heat of the sun. The valley that Osiris presided over was the coolest of the three, even when standing beneath the sun. And the sloping domain of Isis between them was moderate in temperature. With its moderate temperature, this domain was where all wildlife and most plants were found, being spread over with thick [[grass]] and dotted with [[fig]] and [[palm]] trees.{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|20}} Creatures that were known to inhabit Heliopolis included [[lion]]s, [[camel]]s, [[serpent]]s, and [[scorpion]]s. ===World Tree=== Much like the Great Wheel conception of the realm, the Heliopolis of the World Tree (observed by the [[Mulhorandi]] of [[Toril]]) was said to predominantly be a great arid, desert realm where Horus-Re sailed a solar barge across the sky each day. A body of holy water known as the River Isis flowed through the desert, irrigating it and providing a source for all life in the plane. It was also home to oceanus dragons.{{Cite book/Dragons of Faerûn|11}} The land along its banks were a fertile valley named Succor, covered in thick grasses and dotted in both figs and palm trees. Further out beyond the rivers one could find all manner of monuments dotting the desert landscape — mausoleums, obelisks, pyramids, sphinxes, and temples. In the middle of the desert stood a mountain range, the sole source for the rocks used for the plane's monuments. ==Realms== Ra and Osiris were considered to be the dominant powers of Heliopolis, while Isis and Horus held secondary realms.{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|8}} Horus wandered between all three realms, rather than having a realm of his own. * [[Thekele-Re]], the First Realm of Heliopolis, was the domain of Ra. Its primary feature was the Three Pyramids of the Sun. * [[Gizekhtet]], the Second Realm of Heliopolis, was the domain of Isis.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|88}} It housed Isis's temples and the River Isis. * [[Memphiria]], the Third Realm of Heliopolis, was the domain of Osiris.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|90}} It was home to Heliopolis's undead. ==Inhabitants== === Petitioners === Heliopolis was home to petitioners from all many worlds across the [[Prime Material plane]]. The World Tree model, being more Torilian-centric, held that the realm only housed petitioners that were [[Mulhorandi]] in origin. Petitioners in Heliopolis appeared as they did in life, but at their healthiest and most robust. Additionally, in both models the petitioners of Osiris wandered his realm as undead of good alignment, who were treated as no different from the living by the realm's other petitioners. === Planars === Beyond petitioners, one could find the pantheon's unique [[divine minion]]s throughout Heliopolis. Some [[angel]]s and [[lillend]]s served the [[good]] deities of the plane. And a diverse array of horrible creatures could be found in Set's plane of Ankhwugaht. An androsphinx simply known as "The Sphinx" was an indirect proxy of all three rulers of Heliopolis, and of the realm itself. Mortals often sought it out for advice and wisdom.{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|21}} === Powers === The three primary powers of the Pharaonic pantheon - Ra and his great-grandchildren, Isis and Osiris - each ruled their own domain in Heliopolis. Ra goverened the realm as a whole, but delegated rule to Osiris and Isis when dealing with pressing business. Their son Horus had no realm of his own, preferring to roam Heliopolis searching for evil and dish out his brand of justice. The Pharaonic powers [[Set]], [[Geb]] and [[Nut]] once called Heliopolis home. The former was banished for his murder of Osiris,{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|38}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|91}} and the latter pair left after [[Shu]] forbade their marriage. ==Rumors & Legends== Some legends claimed that the great serpent [[Apep]] was buried beneath the sands of Heliopolis. Others claimed that the [[Draconic pantheon|Draconic goddess]] [[Tiamat]] had a home on this plane and maintained a ''[[portal]]'' to another home on the plane of [[Dragon Eyrie]].{{Cite web/Candlekeep forum/Questions for Ed Greenwood (2015)/Tiamat's Many Homes}} When members of the Twisted Rune lich cabal sought her lair, they discovered this to be a ruse, finding in Heliopolis only a cave with a disturbed Netherese lich archwizard spellbound inside, known as the Listener of the Fiveheaded. ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Arcadia}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:Neutral planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Outer Planes]] [[Category:Divine realms]] [[Category:Locations in Buxenus]] [[Category:Locations in Arcadia]] [[Category:Locations in the Upper Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations]]

The '''Heralds of Dust''' (previously '''Dustmen''') are a [[faction]] who believe that the whole multiverse is a sort of purgatory: we're all already dead, although most of us don't realize it. Some -- undead like ghosts or liches or vampires -- are more dead than others, but we're all still stuck here until we can embrace [[True Death]].
== History ==
In the wake of the [[Faction War]] in [[130 YFHR]], most Dustmen shrugged, threw off their faction regalia, and kept doing what they were doing before, as the [[Mortuary Guild]]. "Dustman" becomes Sigilian slang for someone who collects dead bodies.
== Philosophy == We're all dead, some more so than others. We explore our state with patience, purge our passion, and ascend towards the purity of True Death.
== Role ==
The Heralds, as might be expected, run the city's [[Mortuary]], where they come into contact with the dead from all over the city, and ferry them off through one of the city's many portals for disposal. Whether that means burial in [[Elysium]] or cremation in the [[Elemental Plane of Fire]].

The '''Herbivorous Assembly''' is a [[faction]] who don't believe in eating meat, and don't think others should either.
== History ==
Eventually the Vegetarians and the [[Free Flora Collective]] declared war and wiped each other out.
== Philosophy ==
The so-called dumb animals of the multiverse witness everything, so if we could talk to them, we could learn the secrets of the multiverse. Doing something as base as ''eating'' them or killing them for their skin is counter-productive. When everyone in the multiverse has given up eating meat, then everyone will live in harmony and the dark of the multiverse will be revealed.
Some are full vegan, while others are fine eating the products of animal labor like milk or (unfertilized) eggs.

==Description== Hextons were shaped like [[humanoid]]s with long arms and six-fingered hands, as well as four tentacles that ended in sharp claws. They also possessed fan-like wings.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p13-14" />
==Combat== If forced into combat, a hexton used a combination of innate abilities, spells, fists and their sharp claws.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p13-14" />
==Abilities== Like all hierarch modrons, hextons had the innate ability to duplicate the effects of ''[[clairaudience]]'', ''[[clairvoyance]]'', ''[[command]]'', ''[[dimension door]]'', ''[[teleport without error]]'', and ''[[wall of force]]'' spells at will.<ref name="TGMM">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|126}}</ref> Hextons were able to cast [[arcane]] spells as well as [[divine]] spells from the [[Law domain|Law]], [[Protection domain|Protection]] and [[War domain|War]] domains. Hextons were immune to all effects that influenced the mind, all psionic-based attacks and had a resistance to acid, cold and fire.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p13-14" />
==Society== There were only 36 hextons in modron society.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p2" /> They could communicate with other hextons and with [[quinton]]s, and relayed their orders to [[septon]]s. Hextons were the generals of the 36 modron armies. Two of these armies served the [[Secundus|secundi]], three served the [[tertian]]s, sixteen were associated with each of the sixteen regions of [[Mechanus]], and the rest were at the direct disposal of [[Primus]]. Hextons could communicate telepathically with anyone in a 216-mile (348 km) radius.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p13-14" /><ref name="MotPWE3e-p2" />
Hextons were always created as the result of septons being upgraded to take the place of a destroyed hexton, or in case a vacancy appeared due to a hexton being promoted to the rank of quinton.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p2-3">{{Cite web enhancement/The Modrons|2-3}}</ref>
==Ecology== Hextons were able to communicate telepathically with any sentient creature within {{SI|216|mi|k}} and could see in [[darkvision]] up to {{SI|60|ft}}.<ref name="MotPWE3e-p13-14" />
==Notable Hextons== An unidentified rogue hexton owned a shop in [[Sigil]] where it constructed [[steel predator]]s for hire as assassins.<ref name="MTF5e-p239">{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|239}}</ref>

==Location== The exact location of the Hidden Realm within the Outlands was unknown. No maps existed with any information on the realm's whereabouts.<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /> It was speculated that the realm was magically cloaked from detection<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /> or located in a [[demiplane]]<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /><ref name="PGtF-p160" /> connected to the Outlands via a [[portal]].<ref name="PPO2e-p29" />
==Description== The realm itself contained a large crystal tower<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /><ref name="PGtF-p160" /> atop an enormous mountain. From the tower, Annam observed the workings of the [[multiverse]].<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /> The tower contained a great orrery, a model of the [[planes]], the stars, and the planets that simulated their movements perfectly and silently.<ref name="PPO2e-p29" /><ref name="GC2e-p44">{{Cite book/Giantcraft|44}}</ref>
==History== Annam left his original realm of [[Gudheim]] within [[Jotunheim]] as a consequence of his pact with [[Othea]] to abandon the giants until the glory of [[Ostoria]] was restored.<ref name="GC2e-p44" /><ref name="VGM5e-p19">{{Cite book/Volo's Guide to Monsters|19}}</ref> He established himself in the Outlands for the duration of his exile.<ref name="GC2e-p44" />
==Rumors & Legends== It was speculated by some sages that the Hidden Realm, in fact, did not exist. Others argued that the realm itself was the master control of the [[plane]]s.<ref name="PPO2e-p29" />

The entrance was made from red stone and was carved into a screaming [[human]] face. The city was built in a large pit and was unique in that there was only a single road, which spiralled down the pit. At the end of the road was a courtyard which was home of the gate-town's Gate.<ref name="APPttO-p19-20" />
All the buildings of Hopeless were bleak and drab, made from the same gray stone and wood.<ref name="APPttO-p19-20" />
===Gates=== Found at the bottom of the pit, the Gate to Hades appeared as a large well filled with viscous black tar-like ooze. To enter the portal one merely had to jump into the well.<ref name="APPttO-p19-20" />
==Inhabitants== The residents of this gate-town were cheerless and despondent. Individuals who settled in Hopeless were ones who had nowhere else to go and were too depressed to do anything. The Gate to Hades had an effect on the inhabitants as well. Anyone who stayed in the gate-town took on a pallor that matched the drab buildings and their eyes became sensitive to light and bright colors. This transformation began after only a few weeks exposure. Due to the light sensitivity of the residents, a local law forbade bright and contrasting colors.<ref name="APPttO-p19-20" /> ==Appendix== ===References=== {{Refs}}

As a god of justice, he roamed [[Heliopolis]] seeking evildoers and especially the influence of [[Set]]. He achieved his status by punishing Set for murdering his father, and the Defiler never stopped hating him for it.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|88}}</ref>
In the Mulhorandi interpretation of the Pharaonic pantheon, Horus absorbed the power and sphere of Ra (sometimes said to be his father) and was worshipped as '''Horus-Re'''.<ref>{{Cite book/Powers and Pantheons|109}}</ref> An avatar or descendent of Horus led the Mulhorandi in two uprisings against their enslavers, the Imaskar Empire.<ref>{{Cite book/Lost Empires of Faerûn|61}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book/Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide|41}}</ref>

It was home to the deities [[Chauntea]], [[Lathander]], [[Silvanus]], [[Eldath]], [[Gwaeron Windstrom]], [[Lurue]], [[Mielikki]], [[Shiallia]], [[Nobanion]], and [[Ubtao]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|258}} ==Description== While considered a neutral plane by sages, the House of Nature was a place of natural harmony and goodness, encompassing many of the ideals of the plane of [[Elysium]] from the [[Great Wheel cosmology]].The primary natives of [[Elysium]], the [[guardinal]]s, and many of the divine realms of nature deities shifted from Elysium to the House of Nature when the cosmologies were changed between 2{{nd}} and 3{{rd}} edition. A ''[[portal]]'' to the plane of [[Arvandor]] was maintained by cooperation of the deities residing here. ==Flora & Fauna== In addition to all variety of [[animal]]s one might expect to find on a plane of nature, fiercer varieties, such as the [[fhorge]], were plentiful. Strange [[Wood element creature|creatures made entirely of plant and wood]] also inhabited the wilds of this plane. ==Inhabitants== The House of Nature was the native home of the race of [[celestial]]s known as [[guardinal]]s, animalistic beings of inherent goodness. There were also guardinal [[Celestial paragon|paragons]], many in number, who served almost as deities to the plethora of animals populating the plane. These paragons included [[Talisid and the Five Companions]] but were not limited to them.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerun|189}} They focused on defending the House of Nature from the forces of evil. [[Bariaur]]s and [[unicorn]]s also lived here, as did intelligent [[Celestial creature|celestial animals]] who were once natives of the [[Prime Material Plane|Material Plane]]. These [[petitioner]]s of the deities of the House of Nature began their lives here as [[humanoid]]s, but over time, they were changed slowly into animal forms. [[Wemic]] petitioners of Nobanion were an exception; they maintained their wemic forms. The petitioners lived in small communities, never building or changing their environment, but living in complete communion with the natural realm around them. If injured, they healed quickly, and they were immune to electricity and poison and resistant to fire and cold. ==Divine Realms== Many deities and guardinal paragons had realms in the House of Nature. In addition to those described below, [[Animal Lords|animal lords]], such as the [[cat lord]], called the House of Nature Home. So did [[Syranita]], goddess of the [[aarakocra]], [[Skerrit]], god of [[centaur]]s, and other lesser-known deities of nature-oriented races. Gwaeron and Lurue dwelt in the House of Nature, but they did not maintain realms here. The borders of the realms described below were fluid, with hard-to-distinguish boundaries. ===The Deep Forest=== {{Main|Deep Forest}} Silvanus' realm was located in the deepest forest of the House of Nature, where the greatest trees grew so dense as to block out all light. ===The Great Mother's Garden=== {{Main|Great Mother's Garden}} This was the realm of Chauntea. While she was considered a goddess of agriculture, her realm was not, in fact, cultivated. Instead, all manner of foods grew here naturally and in abundance. ===The Grove of the Unicorns=== {{Main|Grove of the Unicorns}} This was a relatively simple tree grove, but it was frequently visited by unicorns, including [[celestial charger]]s. Mielikki maintained her realm here. ===The High Glade=== {{Main|High Glade}} The High Glade, home to Shiallia, was found next to Mielikki's domain. ===The Labyrinth of Life=== {{Main|Labyrinth of Life}} In the warmest region of the House of Nature was found this dense, vibrant, mazelike jungle. This was Ubtao's domain. Bursting up from the center of the jungle was a [[Forbidden Plateau (Labyrinth of Life)|plateau]], upon which all variety of [[dinosaur]]s roamed in isolation from other beasts. ===Morninglory=== {{Main|Morninglory}} The realm of Lathander was a place of natural beauty infused with the colors of dawn and included a mountain lake and a meadow. Here stood a cathedral of tall timber that served as Lathander's home. Anyone resting in Morninglory felt fully refreshed in half the time as usual. ===The Pridelands=== {{Main|Pridelands}} This region of the House of Nature was a vast savanna. Here, Nobanion ruled his wemic petitioners. The savannah was spotted with groves, one of which protected a ''portal'' to the [[Gulthmere Forest]] on the Material Plane. ===The True Grove=== {{Main|True Grove}} Here, Eldath abode in a ring of tall oak trees with a bubbling spring in its center. ==Appendix== ===Notes=== {{Notes}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Neutral planes]] [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Outer Planes]]
